subject: 18E039299C01E45D0C6F1E640C94B63F
introduction: “They forget the kernel but idolize the empty shell.” ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s remarks gathered here are impatient with ritual: religion is not “prayers, fasting and genuflections”, baptism is a symbol whose reality has come, old spiritual exercises are abrogated, kissing of hands and prostration before persons are forbidden, and the Bahá’í Faith “has no set form of public worship”. The Hebrew prophets said it first and most fiercely, Hosea’s “mercy, and not sacrifice”, Isaiah’s “I cannot away with” your solemn meetings; Jesus and Paul continued it; and the Qur’an says righteousness is not in which way one faces. Confucius, the great defender of rites, agrees that they are empty without virtue. Burke’s defence of long-cherished custom and the Christian sense that some rites were commanded are the case for forms.
questions: What do the prophets, and these readings, think goes wrong when ritual is observed carefully?
The Bahá’í Faith has obligatory prayer, a fast and pilgrimage. What distinguishes these from the “worthless rituals” of reading 9?
Burke says we rightly cherish old customs. What human needs do rituals meet, and how might they be met otherwise?
Reading 14 prefers one heartfelt prayer to many pages. How would you apply that to your own practice?

outside.why: When form is given more importance than spirit, people keep the shell and forget the kernel. The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.
Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith.
Clinging to the branch, heedless of the root. I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

Religion does not consist of prayers, fasting and going to mosque. The Qur’an itself: it is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth, and giveth wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy.
Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to deal thy bread to the hungry.
The symbol of baptism is no longer required, its reality being established. Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter.

An infant’s baptism described as a struggle in oily water. Christians hold that Christ commanded such acts: this do in remembrance of me. What does a community lose when it gives up a rite, and what, on the readings’ view, does it gain?
The old spiritual exercises are abrogated. Let no man judge you in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come.
Banish worthless rituals. The new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting.

Immemorial customs hugged like rusty chains. Burke defended exactly this attachment: we cherish our prejudices, and the longer they have lasted the more we cherish them. What is to be said for old forms?
Kissing hands and feet and prostration are forbidden. Paul and Barnabas, when a crowd would have worshipped them: sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you.
No set form of public worship. The true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth.

One foundation under many forms. Confucius, who valued rites more than any teacher, put the condition first: if a man be without the virtues proper to humanity, what has he to do with the rites of propriety? Is that the readings’ position, or a milder one?
Better one prayer of David with supplication than many pages read through. When ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
